lines.required_change: A new file plat/packages/kernel/src/arena/write.ts (M0-a-02's folder; line 2's scope), THE ONE DOOR every arena store passes, exported by path only (rule 5). (a) COLUMN IDS: one per arena column, the per-level ones once per level — vertices x, y, out, level, flags; halfEdges origin, next, prev, level; roles edgeFirst, vertexFirst, kind, entity, level, ordinal, nextInSet, nextSameKey; faces[l] outer, holesStart, holes, kind, owner, parent, stage, nextOfOwner; indexHome vertex, edge, face[l]; roles.head k0, k1, first; faces[l].ownerHead owner, head; handles units, start, hash, slots — and two object ids, p.vertices and p.halfEdges, for the growths that replace those objects whole (plat.ts:360, :368). Each id names a path from the Plat, and `columnOf(p, id)` returns the array the arena holds for it NOW, never an array object kept from earlier (a growth replaces arrays, C-0286 (4)). (b) TYPED SETTERS, one per column id, the column fixed in the function's body (e.g. setVertexX(p, v, x)), in three signature forms: `(p, slot, value)` for the Plat's columns, `(p, level, slot, value)` for faces[l].* and indexHome.face[l], and `(table, slot, value)` for the roles.head, ownerHead and handles columns, whose writers have no Plat in scope and also run on tables no arena owns. Each stores into the column the arena or table holds now and, when that arena's recorder is attached, first appends (column id, slot, old value). A table reaches its arena (and its level, for an owner table) through a registry beside the door — a WeakMap from the table object, filled for p.roles.head, every p.faces[l].ownerHead and p.handles when a recorder is attached and emptied when it is detached (those objects live as long as the arena; growth swaps their arrays, never them); an unregistered table's store is a plain store. No exported signature changes (roleHeadSet, roleHeadDelete, ownerSet, ownerDelete and internId keep theirs). A generic `w(p, id, slot, value)`, or a per-family setter taking a column id, is not the door unless a micro-benchmark in the notes shows it at parity with the typed setters: a direct store, the typed setters and the generic form over one mix of four stores into Int32Array, Uint8Array and Uint16Array columns re-read from the Plat at every store, with no recorder and with one logging, in ns a store over 4·10⁷ stores after a warm-up. (c) THE REPLACEMENT CALL: every assignment that swaps an arena array or table object — a growth, a rehash, the pool compaction's swap — becomes ONE door call, in the Plat-keyed or the table-keyed form as in (b), that, when the recorder is attached, appends (id, the replaced array or object BY REFERENCE) and then assigns. Nothing writes a replaced array after its swap (C-0286 (4)), so the entry holds the content at the swap. Undoing it puts the old array or object back: entries logged before it then replay into the array they were logged against, and entries logged after it are discarded with the new one. Logging every store is correct between two replacements, never across one; with the replacements put back, every column's capacity returns to the mark's. (d) SAVED BY VALUE at a mark, never logged: every SlotCounter WHOLE ({top, free, live} of vertex, pair, face[0..4] and role — allocation reads free before top, plat.ts:449-451); holesTop[0..4] (compactHoles LOWERS it, :693); the version; p.frame (by reference: it is replaced, never mutated); and the COUNTS of roles.head, of each faces[l].ownerHead and of the handle table — `count` fields, not columns, whose stores (tables.ts:113, :144, :193, :219; handles.ts:106) stay as they are and pass no door. (e) THE RECORDER (kernel-internal, by path): `attachRecorder(p)` / `detachRecorder(p)`; `markArena(p)`, returning the log's length, the side list's length and (d)'s values; `undoArena(p, mark)`, which undoes the log's entries ONE AT A TIME from its end down to the mark onto the live arena — a column entry writes its old value into `columnOf(p, id)`, a replacement entry puts its old array or object back — and cuts the log past each entry as soon as it is undone (apply, then cut: the log's and the side list's lengths become that entry's), then restores the mark's (d) values; so an undo a throw interrupts RESUMES at the first entry not yet undone and never re-applies one — a column entry is idempotent only while the array it was logged against is still its column's: re-applied once its rehash or pool swap is back, an entry logged after the swap writes the new array's fill into the old array (tables.ts:90-98, plat.ts:680, :692); a test-only fault hook beside it (null in production, one check for each entry undone), called after each entry's cut, for the pins below; and two read-only accessors for S9: `forEachEntry(p, from, visit)`, which visits the entries logged after the mark `from` in log order — a column entry as (column id, slot, old value), a replacement entry as (id, the replaced reference) — and `entryCounts(p, from)`, which returns { column, replacement } since `from`. The log is parallel typed arrays (id / slot / old, grown by doubling) plus a side list of the replaced references, a replacement entry being one log entry whose old field indexes the side list, so the log's order interleaves both forms. The recorder lives BESIDE the arena — a WeakMap keyed by the Plat, as tx/savepoint.ts keeps TAKEN and RESTORES — never as a Plat field: a Plat that never had a recorder (every Plat in production) is the object it is today, a structuredClone and toEqual see nothing new (facade.test.ts:865-876), and no Map or Set becomes reachable from a Plat (plat.ts:147). A module-level count of attached recorders lets a setter skip the lookup while it is 0, so the production store path is one comparison and the store. (f) WHAT THE LOG IS FOR IN S8: nothing in the kernel reads it in S8 (S9's commit record and size counter will, through forEachEntry / entryCounts). Only the test-side frame observer (line 4) attaches a recorder, and it uses the log to prove, at every in-batch image put-back, that undoArena reproduces the image's arena state — the proof S9 builds on, where undoArena becomes the undo. (g) EVERY STORE IS LOGGED, fresh slots included: S8 builds neither the once-per-slot dedupe nor FRESH skipping — both only cut the undo's cost, which S9 measures, so they are S9's optional optimisations, defined there with the column-to-counter map, the floor and the reset. PINS, kernel/test/tx/door.test.ts (new; default and tiny sizes): every column id's setter stores a sentinel that reads back from the column the id names (a mis-mapped id goes red); with a recorder attached, each setter's entry and each replacement entry is undone by undoArena to its mark, the arena then equal to its mark by line 4's arenaBits — a growth of each slot table, a rehash of roles.head, of an ownerHead and of handles.slots, and a hole-pool compaction among them; an undo the fault hook interrupts right after a roles.head rehash's replacement entries are undone, and one interrupted right after a pool swap is undone (tiny mode), then undoArena to the same mark: arenaBits equals the mark's (its mutant — the log cut only once the whole replay is done, the interrupted undo replayed whole — red); forEachEntry over a frame holding a slot-table growth and a roles.head rehash visits its entries in log order, and entryCounts counts them apart; an unregistered table's store logs nothing; a Plat whose recorder was attached and detached is toEqual and structuredClone-equal to its twin that never had one.

lines.required_change: THE FRAMES, in tx/frames.ts (a-06's; kernel-internal, by path — no folder index or barrel line, rule 5): mark(t) and undoTo(t, m) on the open transaction. A frame is a mark — S8's markArena (arena/write.ts) plus line 2's index mark. undoTo(t, m) undoes every entry above m — undoArena for the arena half, then line 2's index undo — and DISCARDS m and every frame opened after it, as killAfter discards later images (savepoint.ts:140); an op frame's journals are put back by rollback, as today (line 2 (c)). A frame its caller DROPS is committed into its parent implicitly: its entries stay, and it stays on the stack until an undo of an older frame, or the batch's end, discards it — every success path (split.ts:162, claim.ts:199, fan.ts:184 and :332, bandUnion.ts:579), insertCut's refusal after insertChain refused (split.ts:139-142), the over-limit returns inside a frame (claim.ts:185, :195; bandUnion.ts:570) and any frame a throw skips. REFUSED, as a programming error that throws and changes nothing: an undo of a frame already undone or discarded, and an undo from another batch (the LIFO rule is S7's, savepoint.ts:111-149; C-0299 is the restore generation). An undo inside an open batch moves neither the version nor the restore generation (C-0299, C-0313). undoTo cuts each log past each entry as soon as it undoes it (S8's undoArena rule, which line 2's index undo follows too), so an undo a throw interrupts is resumed, never re-applied, by the batch's own undo. lines.required_change: THE FRAME'S STATE, saved at its mark and put back by undoTo. (a) THE ARENA HALF: S8's markArena / undoArena as they stand — every SlotCounter whole, holesTop, the version, the frame and the three tables' counts by value, the column and replacement entries replayed. (b) THE INDEX HALF: record() (spatial.ts:142) gains the GridEntry that gridPut returned for an insert and that gridTake returned for a delete, handed in by gridInsert's and gridDelete's calls (:242, :252) from the `old` they already hold (:239, :249), tombstone's call (:224) passing none — with the IndexWrite field, the two imports and attachIndex's assertion, the only changes to spatial.ts (the scope paragraph). Undoing an insert takes its entry out of the grid (grid.ts gridTake) and, where it replaced an old entry, puts that entry back (gridPut with the old entry's key, partition and box); undoing a delete puts the removed entry back; with each, the partitions' grid shares follow — the key leaves the pending set of the partition its undone entry named and joins the pending set of the partition its restored entry names. A tombstone is undone by deleting its key from its partition's tombstone set (the home entry it cleared is a column store, undone by the arena half). A partition created inside the frame (partitionFor) is undone by truncating idx.partitions, and each level's static and tombstones, to their lengths saved at the mark, and deleting every byKey entry that names a truncated partition — AFTER the writes are undone, since undoing an insert into such a partition reads its pending set first, as gridInsert does (spatial.ts:239-241). idx.work's two counts are saved by value (bits() prints them; savepoint.ts:106-107 restores them). The index undo lives in tx/ and writes the grid (grid.ts gridTake / gridPut), the sets and the lists directly, never through record(); it undoes the IndexBatchLog's writes one at a time from the end and cuts the log past each as soon as it is undone (S8's undoArena rule: an interrupted index undo resumes and never re-applies a write — re-applied, an insert's undo would take the restored old entry out again), the truncation last.
